title: pkix-profiles: an SMTP MTA profile, because BasicTlsProfile silently breaks SMTP DANE
description:
## The trap

verify_smtp_server_dane takes a Profile for DANE-TA(2) path validation. The obvious choice, BasicTlsProfile, sets require_subject_alt_name. That is correct for the Web PKI and wrong for MTA-to-MTA SMTP.

RFC 7672 section 3.2.3 consults the commonName when a certificate presents no DNS-ID, precisely because MTA certificates frequently carry their name only there. A SAN-requiring profile rejects those certificates during PATH VALIDATION, before any name check runs.

The symptom is unhelpfully indirect: Failed(PathValidationFailed(Path(MissingSan))) on a server whose certificate RFC 7672 accepts without reservation. Someone debugging that has no obvious reason to suspect the profile.

## Why this is worth a crate change rather than only documentation

It is documented on verify_smtp_server_dane now, which helps whoever reads the rustdoc. But the failure mode is that a caller reaches for the obvious profile and gets a silent incompatibility with the deployments the feature exists to serve. A shipped profile makes the right choice the easy one.

## What it should assert

Needs deciding rather than guessing:

- require_subject_alt_name: FALSE. This is the whole point.
- EKU: RFC 7672 does not require id-kp-serverAuth. Many MTA certificates carry it, some do not. Requiring it would reject working RFC 7672 deployments, so probably not required -- but worth confirming against what MTAs actually publish.
- Validity dates: DANE-EE(3) skips path validation entirely so dates do not arise. DANE-TA(2) validates a path, so dates apply. RFC 7671 section 5.2 should be read before deciding whether DANE-TA relaxes anything; it was not read during PKIX-rgc6.
- Key sizes and signature algorithms: no reason to differ from the TLS profile.

## Acceptance

[ ] RFC 7671 section 5.2 read and its bearing on DANE-TA date and name checks recorded
[ ] A profile added to pkix-profiles with require_subject_alt_name false, and the EKU question decided with a reason
[ ] verify_smtp_server_dane rustdoc points at it instead of warning about BasicTlsProfile
[ ] pkix-chain/tests/smtp_dane_e2e.rs uses it instead of its locally-defined MtaProfile
close_reason:
FIXED 2026-11-24. pkix_profiles::BasicSmtpMtaProfile, with the open RFC question answered from the text rather than guessed.

## RFC 7671 section 5.2 read, and it relaxes nothing

This bead flagged that section 5.2 had not been read and that DANE-TA date handling was therefore undecided. Read now:

- Section 5.2 grants DANE-TA(2) NO relaxation. It states that "the server certificates will need to have names that match one of the client's reference identifiers", and section 5.2.3 expects a chain that is "signed by the provided public key and has not expired... provided the rest of the chain passes validation, including leaf certificate name checks."
- Section 5.1 is where the relaxation lives, and it is DANE-EE(3) only: "peer identity matching and validity period enforcement are based solely on the TLSA RRset properties", and "The server MUST be considered authenticated even if none of the names in the certificate match the client's reference identity."

So dates and names are enforced normally for DANE-TA(2). DANE-EE(3) relaxes both, and in this workspace it does so by validating no path at all, which means no profile is consulted for it. The profile therefore relaxes exactly two things and nothing more.

## The EKU question, decided with a reason rather than a preference

Not required. Three reasons, in increasing order of how concrete they are:

1. RFC 7672 imposes no EKU requirement.
2. RFC 5280 section 4.2.1.12 treats an absent EKU as unrestricted, so requiring id-kp-serverAuth would be stricter than RFC 5280 itself.
3. Decisively: required_leaf_eku is NOT satisfied by an absent EKU extension. pkix-path's own test pins this -- "required_leaf_eku=Some([serverAuth]) with absent EKU -> MissingEku" -- and self-managed MTA certificates commonly carry no EKU at all. Requiring it would reject exactly the certificates DANE makes usable without a public CA.

A deployment that knows its peers all publish serverAuth can add the requirement to the returned policy. It is not the default because the default has to work for the general case.

## Tested behaviourally, not by asserting policy fields

The valuable tests are the contrasts, using existing pkix-path fixtures:

- leaf-p256-365d-no-san.der validates under this profile and fails BasicTlsProfile with MissingSan
- leaf-p256-365d-no-eku.der validates under this profile and fails BasicTlsProfile with MissingEku

Asserting the policy flags alone would pass against a profile that was correct in its fields and wrong in its effect. Two further tests cover the absences directly, since both are things a later edit could re-add and nothing else here would catch, and one confirms an EXPIRED chain still fails -- the easy mistake in a deliberately permissive profile is relaxing one thing too many.

## Naming and scope

BasicSmtpMtaProfile rather than BasicSmtpProfile, because RFC 7672 section 3.1.3 explicitly puts MUA-to-MSA submission on ports 587 and 465 out of scope and a bare "Smtp" would imply a claim about them. id is "ietf.smtp-mta-dane", following the reverse-domain convention of the other profiles. The basic_smtp_mta_policy free function follows the existing alias pattern.

## Acceptance

[x] RFC 7671 section 5.2 read and its bearing recorded -- no relaxation for DANE-TA, and section 5.1 is where DANE-EE's relaxation lives
[x] Profile added with require_subject_alt_name false, and the EKU question decided with a reason
[x] verify_smtp_server_dane rustdoc points at it instead of warning about BasicTlsProfile
[x] pkix-chain/tests/smtp_dane_e2e.rs uses it; the local MtaProfile stand-in is gone

## Noted, not done

No LintProfile impl. BasicTlsProfile and BasicSmimeProfile have one; the obvious candidate lint for a TLS server certificate is Rfc6125TlsServerSanLint, which asserts the SAN requirement this profile deliberately drops, so the right lint set here is not simply a subset of an existing one. Left out rather than assembled on a guess; worth a small follow-up if shape-checking SMTP certificates turns out to be wanted.
